can_baud_rate.name: can_baud_rate
can_baud_rate.label: CAN Baud Rate
can_baud_rate.help: The baud rate of the CAN-Bus. Note that all devices on the bus must have the same baud rate.

pairing_done.name: pairing_done
pairing_done.label: Pairing Done
pairing_done.help: Pairing done flag. If this flag is set, a bluetooth connection can only be made if the VESC Tool instance making the connection has been paired to this VESC. The pairing is done by storing the UUID of the VESC in the pairing list.

permanent_uart_enabled.name: permanent_uart_enabled
permanent_uart_enabled.label: Enable Permanent UART
permanent_uart_enabled.help: Enable the permanent UART port (if the hardware has one). This port can be connected to e.g. the NRF51 for providing a BLE link. You may want to disable this to prevent access to your VESC over BLE.

shutdown_mode.name: shutdown_mode
shutdown_mode.label: Shutdown Mode
shutdown_mode.help:
Shutdown mode for hardware that supports it (such as the VESC HD). Determines how the VESC shuts itself off, which eliminates the need for an external switch.

NOTE: Most VESCs with this feature also support push to start, which means that the VESC will switch on as soon as the motor is turned at a minimum speed.

The available modes are:

ALWAYS_OFF

The VESC power is only determined by the inverted state of the shutdown input.

ALWAYS_ON

The VESC always stays on after being powered.

TOGGLE_BUTTON_ONLY

A normally closed (NC) momentary button can be connected to the shutdown input to toggle the power on or off. The VESC will sample the button and determine whether it is pressed, which can be used to shut down after the button is released.

OFF_AFTER_x

Same as the TOGGLE_BUTTON_ONLY mode, but the VESC will shut down after X time of inactivity. This mode is useful for setups without any switch at all if the hardware supports push to start, such as the VESC HD.

can_mode.name: can_mode
can_mode.label: CAN Mode
can_mode.help:
CAN-bus mode.

VESC

Default VESC CAN-bus. Required for CAN forwarding and configuring multiple VESCs using VESC Tool.

UAVCAN

Basic implementation of UAVCAN. Currently needs some work.

Comm Brigde

Bridge CAN-bus to commands. Useful for using the VESC and VESC Tool as a generic CAN interface and debugger.

Unused

CAN-frames are not processed at all and just ignored. Custom applications and scripts can still process CAN-frames. This is very similar to Comm Bridge, but the received frames are not forwarded using commands.

UAVCAN and VESC

Experimental mode where frames that aren't processed by UAVCAN are processed by the VESC decoder. This can give limited VESC Tool configuration support on UAVCAN networks.

uavcan_raw_mode.name: uavcan_raw_mode
uavcan_raw_mode.label: UAVCAN Raw Throttle Mode
uavcan_raw_mode.help:
Drive mode for the raw throttle command in UAVCAN.

Current Control

The raw command corresponds to a fraction of the configured current limit. 1.0 is maximum current forwards and -1.0 is maximum current reverse.

Current No Reverse Brake

Same as current control, but negative values only give braking and don't start the motor in the other direction.

Duty Cycle Control

Duty cycle control.

RPM Control

RPM control. Use the raw command times the maximum configured ERPM value. Negative values will run the motor in reverse. Note that this will set the value in ERPM, so the RPM will be scaled by the number of pole pairs.

uavcan_raw_rpm_max.name: uavcan_raw_rpm_max
uavcan_raw_rpm_max.label: UAVCAN Raw RPM Max
uavcan_raw_rpm_max.help: Maximum ERPM for the RPM mode of the raw command.

uavcan_status_current_mode.name: uavcan_status_current_mode
uavcan_status_current_mode.label: UAVCAN Status Current Mode
uavcan_status_current_mode.help: Current to send in status message.

servo_out_enable.name: servo_out_enable
servo_out_enable.label: Enable Servo Output
servo_out_enable.help: Enable servo output on PPM-port when PPM-app is disabled.

kill_sw_mode.name: kill_sw_mode
kill_sw_mode.label: Kill Switch Mode
kill_sw_mode.help:
Kill switch input. When this input is active the motor is disabled and optionally braking if timeout_brake_current is greater than 0. The kill switch overrides all other inputs and can be used as an emergency stop.

The following modes can be used:

Disabled

No kill switch is used.

PPM Low

The kill switch is active when the PPM input goes low.

PPM High

The kill switch is active when the PPM input goes high.

ADC2 Low

The kill switch is active when the ADC2 input goes low.

ADC2 High

The kill switch is active when the ADC2 input goes high.

app_to_use.name: app_to_use
app_to_use.label: APP to Use
app_to_use.help: The APP to use. With multiple VESC connected over CAN only the master needs to have an app to use set up. Notice that using the NRF nunchuk needs the NRF app.

app_ppm_conf.ctrl_type.name: app_ppm_conf.ctrl_type
app_ppm_conf.ctrl_type.label: Control Type
app_ppm_conf.ctrl_type.help:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Current

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, at which point it starts in the reverse direction.

Current No Reverse

Current control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current No Reverse With Brake

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, but not further.

Duty Cycle

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center gives negative duty cycle.

Duty Cycle No Reverse

Duty cycle control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

PID Speed Control

PID speed control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center gives negative set speed.

PID Speed Control No Reverse

Duty cycle control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current Hyst Reverse With Brake

Current Hyst Reverse With Brake. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, at which point it starts in the reverse direction, but if Max dir switch ERPM is enabled it will stop the reverse when it reaches the Max ERPM for direction switch.

Current Smart Reverse

Similar to the Current No Reverse With Brake mode, but holding full brake will switch to duty cycle mode in the reverse direction when the speed is so low that not enough brake torque can be produced. This is useful when trying to stop downhill where you normally would roll forwards slowly even at full brake. Instead, the board will start to go reverse slowly in duty cycle mode if this mode is activated.

PID Position Control: 180°

Maps servo input to (-180° <> +180°) rotation. Remote should center at “Pulselegth Center” value.

Motor will rotate ±180° from the starting position.

PID Position Control: 360°
Maps servo input to (+0 <> +360°) rotation. Remote should center at “Pulselegth Start” value.
Motor will rotate up to +360° from the starting position. It will only rotate in the "positive" direction from the starting position.

PID Position Control notes:
Servo like position control of motor. Works best with an encoder, but can work with HFI.

Angle division:

• To get multiple turns of the motor for full stick movement, adjust: “Motor Settings” -> “PID Controllers” -> “Position Angle Division” to greater than 1.

• For setups with angle division > 1, you will need to “home” your motor manually to the right “zero” rotation before power on.

• To get less than 1 full turn, set “Position Angle Division” to less than 1.

Starting position:

• To adjust the starting position of the motor, adjust: “Motor Settings” -> “PID Controllers” -> “Position PID Offset Angle”.

• This will change the zero angle AFTER the angle division has been applied. To change the angle by 90° with an angle division of 2, this should be 45°.

Safe Start:

Safe start still works with PID Position Control, with an additional safety step.

To start the motor with Safe Start, you must:

• Set ppm to your “center” value:

• “Pulselegth Center” for 180 mode.

• “Pulselegth Start” for 360 mode.

• Note: disabling "Safe Start" will eliminate this step but not the second step.

• Bring your commanded angle close to the actual motor angle.

• This can be done by sweeping the stick the full range until the motor starts tracking.

• This is done to prevent a rapid movement at start to a far off commanded pid angle.

app_ppm_conf.pid_max_erpm.name: app_ppm_conf.pid_max_erpm
app_ppm_conf.pid_max_erpm.label: PID Max ERPM
app_ppm_conf.pid_max_erpm.help: The ERPM setpoint corresponding to max input when using PID Speed Control.

app_ppm_conf.pulse_start.name: app_ppm_conf.pulse_start
app_ppm_conf.pulse_start.label: Pulselength Start
app_ppm_conf.pulse_start.help: The shortest pulse length for the PPM input in milliseconds. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the minimum input.

app_ppm_conf.pulse_end.name: app_ppm_conf.pulse_end
app_ppm_conf.pulse_end.label: Pulselength End
app_ppm_conf.pulse_end.help: The longest pulse length for the PPM input in milliseconds. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the maximum input.

app_ppm_conf.pulse_center.name: app_ppm_conf.pulse_center
app_ppm_conf.pulse_center.label: Pulselength Center
app_ppm_conf.pulse_center.help: The PPM input in milliseconds at which the throttle is centered. Can be checked by enabling display and leaving the throttle centered. This setting has no effect in control modes where the output is not off when the stick is centered.

app_ppm_conf.median_filter.name: app_ppm_conf.median_filter
app_ppm_conf.median_filter.label: Median Filter
app_ppm_conf.median_filter.help: Use a median filter on the decoded pulses. Will delay the signal slightly, but rejects outliers caused by noise.

app_ppm_conf.safe_start.name: app_ppm_conf.safe_start
app_ppm_conf.safe_start.label: Safe Start
app_ppm_conf.safe_start.help:
Prevent motor from starting in some unsafe conditions. Modes:

Disabled

Motor can always start.

Regular

Only allow starting the motor when the input has beed zero for long enough after boot, after configuration updates and after faults.

No Faults

Same as regular, but the motor can start directly after fault codes are cleared.

app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp.name: app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp
app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp.label: Throttle Expo
app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp.help:
Exponential gain for the throttle.

Zero (0)

Linear throttle

Negative (<0)

The throttle is softer close to 0 and increases exponentially towards full throttle.

Positive (>0)

The throttle reacts fast around 0 and decreases exponentially towards full throttle.

Increasing the magnitude of this value will increase the exponential effect. The full throttle curve can be seen in the throttle curve plot.

app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_brake.name: app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_brake
app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_brake.label: Throttle Expo Brake
app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_brake.help:
Exponential gain for the throttle.

Zero (0)

Linear throttle

Negative (<0)

The throttle is softer close to 0 and increases exponentially towards full throttle.

Positive (>0)

The throttle reacts fast around 0 and decreases exponentially towards full throttle.

Increasing the magnitude of this value will increase the exponential effect. The full throttle curve can be seen in the throttle curve plot.

app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_mode.name: app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_mode
app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_mode.label: Throttle Expo Mode
app_ppm_conf.throttle_exp_mode.help:
The throttle curve mode.

Exponential

y = x^(1 + c)

Natural

y = (e^(cx) - 1) / (e^c - 1)

Polynomial

y = x / (1 + c(1 - x))

where

y: output

x: input

c: curve

The curve parameter, offsets and signs are mapped accordingly for each mode.

app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_pos.name: app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_pos
app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_pos.label: Positive Ramping Time
app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_pos.help: Positive ramping time constant. This filters the input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from zero to full output.

app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_neg.name: app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_neg
app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_neg.label: Negative Ramping Time
app_ppm_conf.ramp_time_neg.help: Negative ramping time constant. This filters the input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from full output (acceleration or braking) back to zero.

app_ppm_conf.multi_esc.name: app_ppm_conf.multi_esc
app_ppm_conf.multi_esc.label: Multiple VESCs Over CAN
app_ppm_conf.multi_esc.help: Listen for other VESCs on the CAN-bus and send the same control commands to them. Notice that the application only has to be set up on the master VESC.

app_ppm_conf.tc.name: app_ppm_conf.tc
app_ppm_conf.tc.label: Traction Control
app_ppm_conf.tc.help: Enable traction control between multiple VESCs connected over CAN-bus. This is only used for current control modes.

app_ppm_conf.tc_max_diff.name: app_ppm_conf.tc_max_diff
app_ppm_conf.tc_max_diff.label: TC Max ERPM Difference
app_ppm_conf.tc_max_diff.help: The ERPM difference at which the fastest motor gets swtiched off completely. If the difference in ERPM is lower than that the current to faster motors is scaled down proportionally to the difference.

app_ppm_conf.max_erpm_for_dir.name: app_ppm_conf.max_erpm_for_dir
app_ppm_conf.max_erpm_for_dir.label: Max ERPM for direction switch
app_ppm_conf.max_erpm_for_dir.help: The Max ERPM where the direction can be switched to reverse by braking 2 times.

app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.name: app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_max_duty
app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.label: Smart Reverse Max Duty Cycle
app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.help: Maximum duty cycle to use in smart reverse mode.

app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.name: app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time
app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.label: Smart Reverse Ramp Time
app_ppm_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.help: Time to ramp to maximum duty cycle in smart reverse mode.

app_adc_conf.ctrl_type.name: app_adc_conf.ctrl_type
app_adc_conf.ctrl_type.label: Control Type
app_adc_conf.ctrl_type.help:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Current

Current control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current Reverse Center

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, at which point it it starts in the reverse direction.

Current Reverse Button

Current control with a button for reversing the throttle. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current Reverse ADC2 Brake Button

Current control with a button for reversing the throttle. The output is off when the input is at minimum. The second ADC channel acts as a brake.

Current Reverse Button Brake Center

Current control with a button for reversing throttle. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, but not further.

Current No Reverse Brake Center

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center brakes until the motor stops, but not further.

Current No Reverse Brake Button

Current control with a button for turning the throttle into a brake. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Current No Reverse Brake ADC2

Current control with one separate throttle connected to ADC2 for braking.

Duty Cycle

Duty cycle control. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

Duty Cycle Reverse Center

Current control. The output is off when the input is centered. Input less than center gives negative duty cycle.

Duty Cycle Reverse Button

Duty cycle control with a button on UART RX for inverting the throttle. The output is off when the input is at minimum.

PID Speed

PID speed control. The speed setpoint is mapped between 0 and the configured maximum motor speed limit.

PID Speed Reverse Center

PID speed control. The output is mapped between the minimum and maximum motor speed limits. Throttle center corresponds to 0 speed.

PID Speed Reverse Button

PID speed control with a button for reversing the throttle. The speed setpoint is mapped between 0 and the configured maximum motor speed limit, or between 0 and the minimum motor speed limit when the UART RX input is high.

app_adc_conf.voltage_start.name: app_adc_conf.voltage_start
app_adc_conf.voltage_start.label: ADC1 Start Voltage
app_adc_conf.voltage_start.help: Input voltage at the start of the throttle range for ADC1. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the minimum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.voltage_end.name: app_adc_conf.voltage_end
app_adc_conf.voltage_end.label: ADC1 End Voltage
app_adc_conf.voltage_end.help: Input voltage at the end of the throttle range for ADC1. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the maximum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.voltage_min.name: app_adc_conf.voltage_min
app_adc_conf.voltage_min.label: ADC1 Abs Min Voltage
app_adc_conf.voltage_min.help: Minimum valid voltage on ADC1. If the voltage is below this value the motor will be stopped and if safe start is activated the throttle must be returned to 0 before the motor is allowed to run again.

app_adc_conf.voltage_max.name: app_adc_conf.voltage_max
app_adc_conf.voltage_max.label: ADC1 Abs Max Voltage
app_adc_conf.voltage_max.help: Maximum valid voltage on ADC1. If the voltage is above this value the motor will be stopped and if safe start is activated the throttle must be returned to 0 before the motor is allowed to run again.

app_adc_conf.voltage_center.name: app_adc_conf.voltage_center
app_adc_conf.voltage_center.label: ADC1 Center Voltage
app_adc_conf.voltage_center.help:
Input voltage at the center of the throttle range for ADC1. Can be checked by enabling display and centering the input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

Notice that this parameter only is used for the contered control types. For the other types the voltage will always be mapped linearly between start and end.

app_adc_conf.voltage2_start.name: app_adc_conf.voltage2_start
app_adc_conf.voltage2_start.label: ADC2 Start Voltage
app_adc_conf.voltage2_start.help: Input voltage at the start of the throttle range for ADC2. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the minimum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.voltage2_end.name: app_adc_conf.voltage2_end
app_adc_conf.voltage2_end.label: ADC2 End Voltage
app_adc_conf.voltage2_end.help: Input voltage at the end of the throttle range for ADC2. Can be checked by enabling display and giving the maximum input. If Control Type is set to off while doing that the motor won't turn.

app_adc_conf.use_filter.name: app_adc_conf.use_filter
app_adc_conf.use_filter.label: Use Filter
app_adc_conf.use_filter.help: Use a low-pass filter to reject noise. This will introduce a slight delay.

app_adc_conf.safe_start.name: app_adc_conf.safe_start
app_adc_conf.safe_start.label: Safe Start
app_adc_conf.safe_start.help:
Prevent motor from starting in some unsafe conditions. Modes:

Disabled

Motor can always start.

Regular

Only allow starting the motor when the input has beed zero for long enough after boot, after configuration updates and after faults.

No Faults

Same as regular, but the motor can start directly after fault codes are cleared.

app_adc_conf.buttons.name: app_adc_conf.buttons
app_adc_conf.buttons.label: Button Inputs
app_adc_conf.buttons.help:
A cruise control and a reverse button can be used with the ADC app. The reverse button is only used on the control modes that have button in their name, but cruise control can be used on all control modes when enabled. The buttons can be connected as follows:

Comm TX: Cruise Control

Comm RX: Reverse

If the UART app is active the PPM-input is used for the button instead. That means you only have one button, which will be the reverse button for the button-modes (not cruise control available) or cruise control for non-button control modes.

By default the button inputs have a pull-up resistor and are active low.

Enable Cruise Control

Enable cruise control button input.

Invert CC Button

Invert the polarity of the cruise control button.

Invert Reverse Button

Invert the polarity of the reverse button.

app_adc_conf.ramp_time_pos.name: app_adc_conf.ramp_time_pos
app_adc_conf.ramp_time_pos.label: Positive Ramping Time
app_adc_conf.ramp_time_pos.help: Positive ramping time constant. This filters the input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from zero to full output.

app_adc_conf.ramp_time_neg.name: app_adc_conf.ramp_time_neg
app_adc_conf.ramp_time_neg.label: Negative Ramping Time
app_adc_conf.ramp_time_neg.help: Negative ramping time constant. This filters the input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from full output (acceleration or braking) back to zero.

app_adc_conf.multi_esc.name: app_adc_conf.multi_esc
app_adc_conf.multi_esc.label: Multiple VESCs Over CAN
app_adc_conf.multi_esc.help: Listen for other VESCs on the CAN-bus and send the same control commands to them. Notice that the application only has to be set up on the master VESC.

app_adc_conf.tc.name: app_adc_conf.tc
app_adc_conf.tc.label: Traction Control
app_adc_conf.tc.help: Enable traction control between multiple VESCs connected over CAN-bus. This is only is only used for current control modes.

app_adc_conf.tc_max_diff.name: app_adc_conf.tc_max_diff
app_adc_conf.tc_max_diff.label: TC Max ERPM Difference
app_adc_conf.tc_max_diff.help: The ERPM difference at which the fastest motor gets swtiched off completely. If the difference in ERPM is lower than that the current to faster motors is scaled down proportionally to the difference.

app_adc_conf.update_rate_hz.name: app_adc_conf.update_rate_hz
app_adc_conf.update_rate_hz.label: Update Rate
app_adc_conf.update_rate_hz.help: Rate at which the input is sampled.

app_chuk_conf.ctrl_type.name: app_chuk_conf.ctrl_type
app_chuk_conf.ctrl_type.label: Control Type
app_chuk_conf.ctrl_type.help:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Current

Current control. The output is off when the joystick is centered. Positive input gives acceleration and negative input braking. To go reverse the Z button can be used to toggle direction.

Current No Reverse

Current control. The output is off when the joystick is centered. Positive input gives acceleration and negative input braking. The reverse function of the Z button is disabled.

Current Bidirectional

Current control. The output is off when the joystick is centered. Positive input always gives forward current and negative current always gives reverse current. This means that when current is applied through 0 speed, the motor will accelerate in the other direction.

app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_pos.name: app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_pos
app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_pos.label: Positive Ramping Time
app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_pos.help: Positive ramping time constant. This filters the joystick input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from zero to full output.

app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_neg.name: app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_neg
app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_neg.label: Negative Ramping Time
app_chuk_conf.ramp_time_neg.help: Negative ramping time constant. This filters the joystick input with ramping. This constant represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from full output (acceleration or braking) back to zero.

app_chuk_conf.stick_erpm_per_s_in_cc.name: app_chuk_conf.stick_erpm_per_s_in_cc
app_chuk_conf.stick_erpm_per_s_in_cc.label: ERPM Per Second Cruise Control
app_chuk_conf.stick_erpm_per_s_in_cc.help: The amount of ERPM per second the setpoint changes when giving full joystick input with criuse control activated.

app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp.name: app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp
app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp.label: Throttle Expo
app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp.help:
Exponential gain for the throttle.

Zero (0)

Linear throttle

Negative (<0)

The throttle is softer close to 0 and increases exponentially towards full throttle.

Positive (>0)

The throttle reacts fast around 0 and decreases exponentially towards full throttle.

Increasing the magnitude of this value will increase the exponential effect. The full throttle curve can be seen in the throttle curve plot.

app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_brake.name: app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_brake
app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_brake.label: Throttle Expo Brake
app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_brake.help:
Exponential gain for the throttle.

Zero (0)

Linear throttle

Negative (<0)

The throttle is softer close to 0 and increases exponentially towards full throttle.

Positive (>0)

The throttle reacts fast around 0 and decreases exponentially towards full throttle.

Increasing the magnitude of this value will increase the exponential effect. The full throttle curve can be seen in the throttle curve plot.

app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_mode.name: app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_mode
app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_mode.label: Throttle Expo Mode
app_chuk_conf.throttle_exp_mode.help:
The throttle curve mode.

Exponential

y = x^(1 + c)

Natural

y = (e^(cx) - 1) / (e^c - 1)

Polynomial

y = x / (1 + c(1 - x))

where

y: output

x: input

c: curve

The curve parameter, offsets and signs are mapped accordingly for each mode.

app_chuk_conf.multi_esc.name: app_chuk_conf.multi_esc
app_chuk_conf.multi_esc.label: Multiple VESCs Over CAN
app_chuk_conf.multi_esc.help: Listen for other VESCs on the CAN-bus and send the same control commands to them. Notice that the application only has to be set up on the master VESC.

app_chuk_conf.tc.name: app_chuk_conf.tc
app_chuk_conf.tc.label: Traction Control
app_chuk_conf.tc.help: Enable traction control between multiple VESCs connected over CAN-bus. This is only is only used for current control modes.

app_chuk_conf.tc_max_diff.name: app_chuk_conf.tc_max_diff
app_chuk_conf.tc_max_diff.label: TC Max ERPM Difference
app_chuk_conf.tc_max_diff.help: The ERPM difference at which the fastest motor gets swtiched off completely. If the difference in ERPM is lower than that the current to faster motors is scaled down proportionally to the difference.

app_chuk_conf.use_smart_rev.name: app_chuk_conf.use_smart_rev
app_chuk_conf.use_smart_rev.label: Use Smart Reverse
app_chuk_conf.use_smart_rev.help:
Use smart reverse function. If enabled, holding full brake will switch to duty cycle mode in the reverse direction when the speed is so low that not enough brake torque can be produced.

This is useful when trying to stop downhill where you normally would roll forwards slowly even at full brake. Instead, the board will start to go reverse slowly in duty cycle mode if this mode is activated.

app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.name: app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_max_duty
app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.label: Smart Reverse Max Duty Cycle
app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_max_duty.help: Maximum duty cycle to use in smart reverse mode.

app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.name: app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time
app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.label: Smart Reverse Ramp Time
app_chuk_conf.smart_rev_ramp_time.help: Time to ramp to maximum duty cycle in smart reverse mode.

app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_level.name: app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_level
app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_level.label: Coasting Brake Level
app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_level.help: Coasting brake level. Brake with this fraction of the braking current when the throttle is released.

app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_ramp_time.name: app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_ramp_time
app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_ramp_time.label: Coasting Brake Ramp Time
app_chuk_conf.coast_brake_ramp_time.help: Time to ramp to maximum coasting brake when releasing the throttle.

app_nrf_conf.power.name: app_nrf_conf.power
app_nrf_conf.power.label: TX Power
app_nrf_conf.power.help: Transmit power or power off setting.

app_nrf_conf.retry_delay.name: app_nrf_conf.retry_delay
app_nrf_conf.retry_delay.label: Retry Delay
app_nrf_conf.retry_delay.help: Delay between retries when no ack is received. If the speed is lower than 2MBit, at least 500 µS should be used.

app_nrf_conf.retries.name: app_nrf_conf.retries
app_nrf_conf.retries.label: Retries
app_nrf_conf.retries.help: Maximum number of retries when no ack is received before giving up on the current packet.

app_nrf_conf.send_crc_ack.name: app_nrf_conf.send_crc_ack
app_nrf_conf.send_crc_ack.label: Send ACK
app_nrf_conf.send_crc_ack.help: Send ACK when valid packets are received.

app_pas_conf.ctrl_type.name: app_pas_conf.ctrl_type
app_pas_conf.ctrl_type.label: Control Type
app_pas_conf.ctrl_type.help:
Off

The output is switched off regardless of the input.

Cadence

Cadence control. The output is proportional to the pedalling speed, off when there is no pedalling.

Constant Torque

Constant Torque control. Pedalling provides constant output, off when no pedalling. Suited for gearless setup.

app_pas_conf.sensor_type.name: app_pas_conf.sensor_type
app_pas_conf.sensor_type.label: Sensor Type
app_pas_conf.sensor_type.help:
Quadrature

This interface provides 2 signals that can be decoded to know the pedalling direction (forward of backwards).

app_pas_conf.current_scaling.name: app_pas_conf.current_scaling
app_pas_conf.current_scaling.label: PAS Max Current
app_pas_conf.current_scaling.help: Maximum PAS output current will be limited to this percentage of the global output current.

app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_start.name: app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_start
app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_start.label: Pedal RPM Start
app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_start.help: Pedal RPM at which the assist starts. Below this value the output current is zero.

app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_end.name: app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_end
app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_end.label: Pedal RPM End
app_pas_conf.pedal_rpm_end.help: Pedal RPM at which the assist stops increasing. Above this pedal speed the assist output will stay at its maximum.

app_pas_conf.magnets.name: app_pas_conf.magnets
app_pas_conf.magnets.label: Sensor Magnets
app_pas_conf.magnets.help:
How many magnets the PAS sensor assembly has. 24 magnets would provide 24 pulses per pedal revolution.

12 and 24 magnet setups are typical.

app_pas_conf.use_filter.name: app_pas_conf.use_filter
app_pas_conf.use_filter.label: Use Filter
app_pas_conf.use_filter.help: Use a low pass filter in the PAS input signal

app_pas_conf.ramp_time_pos.name: app_pas_conf.ramp_time_pos
app_pas_conf.ramp_time_pos.label: Positive Ramping Time
app_pas_conf.ramp_time_pos.help: Positive ramping time constant. This filters the PAS input with ramping and represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from zero to full output.

app_pas_conf.ramp_time_neg.name: app_pas_conf.ramp_time_neg
app_pas_conf.ramp_time_neg.label: Negative Ramping Time
app_pas_conf.ramp_time_neg.help: Negative ramping time constant. This filters the PAS input with ramping and represents the amount of secods it takes to ramp from full to zero output.

app_pas_conf.update_rate_hz.name: app_pas_conf.update_rate_hz
app_pas_conf.update_rate_hz.label: Update Rate
app_pas_conf.update_rate_hz.help: Frequency at which the PAS control loop is executed

imu_conf.type.name: imu_conf.type
imu_conf.type.label: IMU Type
imu_conf.type.help: IMU type. The internal IMU is only available if the hardware supports it. External IMUs can be connected to the SDA and SCL pins. If using an external IMU, make sure that no app that uses the same pins is selected.

imu_conf.mode.name: imu_conf.mode
imu_conf.mode.label: IMU AHRS Mode
imu_conf.mode.help: Use the Madgwick or Mahony AHRS filter.

imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_x.name: imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_x
imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_x.label: Accel lowpass filter X
imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_x.help:
Accelerometer lowpass filter

Biquad lowpass filter applied to X axis. This is run on the ESC and will be applied regardless of IMU model.

Setting the filter to 0Hz will disable it.

imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_y.name: imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_y
imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_y.label: Accel lowpass filter Y
imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_y.help:
Accelerometer lowpass filter

Biquad lowpass filter applied to Y axis. This is run on the ESC and will be applied regardless of IMU model.

Setting the filter to 0Hz will disable it.

imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_z.name: imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_z
imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_z.label: Accel lowpass filter Z
imu_conf.accel_lowpass_filter_z.help:
Accelerometer lowpass filter

Biquad lowpass filter applied to Z axis. This is run on the ESC and will be applied regardless of IMU model.

Setting the filter to 0Hz will disable it.

imu_conf.gyro_lowpass_filter.name: imu_conf.gyro_lowpass_filter
imu_conf.gyro_lowpass_filter.label: Gyro lowpass filter
imu_conf.gyro_lowpass_filter.help:
Gyrosocpe lowpass filter

Biquad lowpass filter applied to all 3 axes of the gyroscope. This is run on the ESC and will be applied regardless of IMU model.

Setting the filter to 0Hz will disable it.

imu_conf.sample_rate_hz.name: imu_conf.sample_rate_hz
imu_conf.sample_rate_hz.label: Sample Rate
imu_conf.sample_rate_hz.help: IMU sample rate. Higher sample rates use more CPU cycles, but perform better.

imu_conf.accel_confidence_decay.name: imu_conf.accel_confidence_decay
imu_conf.accel_confidence_decay.label: Accelerometer Confidence Decay
imu_conf.accel_confidence_decay.help: This factor sets how fast the accelerometer confidence will be decreased if the acceleration vector differs from 1.0.

imu_conf.mahony_kp.name: imu_conf.mahony_kp
imu_conf.mahony_kp.label: Mahony KP
imu_conf.mahony_kp.help: KP for Mahony filter. Decides how much the accelerometer is used for attitude estimation. Increasing this value helps against gyro offsets, but makes the output noisier.

imu_conf.mahony_ki.name: imu_conf.mahony_ki
imu_conf.mahony_ki.label: Mahony KI
imu_conf.mahony_ki.help: KI for Mahony filter. Integrates gyro offsets over time.

imu_conf.madgwick_beta.name: imu_conf.madgwick_beta
imu_conf.madgwick_beta.label: Madgwick Beta
imu_conf.madgwick_beta.help: Beta for Madgwick filter. Decides how much the accelerometer is used for attitude estimation. Increasing this value helps against gyro offsets, but makes the output noisier.

imu_conf.rot_roll.name: imu_conf.rot_roll
imu_conf.rot_roll.label: Imu Rotation Roll
imu_conf.rot_roll.help: Roll rotation of IMU. Can be adjusted if the IMU is not aligned with the vehicle.

imu_conf.rot_pitch.name: imu_conf.rot_pitch
imu_conf.rot_pitch.label: Imu Rotation Pitch
imu_conf.rot_pitch.help: Pitch rotation of IMU. Can be adjusted if the IMU is not aligned with the vehicle.

imu_conf.rot_yaw.name: imu_conf.rot_yaw
imu_conf.rot_yaw.label: Imu Rotation Yaw
imu_conf.rot_yaw.help: Yaw rotation of IMU. Can be adjusted if the IMU is not aligned with the vehicle.
